text:
Tasha: Heads-up — I'm seeing a spike where requests are routed to the smaller model-quant variant even though decision logs show fallback=false. Noticed this around 09:06-09:12 UTC. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/route-eval. Anyone seen this pattern?

Mike: Can you paste one raw request header + the decision_log entry for a sample request? My first guess is header-override happening after we emit the decision log.

Tasha: Here's one example (sanitized):
```
Request headers:
  :method: POST
  :path: /v1/generate
  authorization: Bearer REDACTED
  x-customer-tier: enterprise
  x-routing-override: model=small-quant

DecisionLog entry:
  route_id: gen-default
  selected_model: large-1.2b
  fallback: false
  sampling_key: session:abcd1234
  trace_id: -
```

Olivia: That looks like the root cause pattern we've discussed — header overrides are applied in the routing middleware that runs after decision_log emission for performance reasons. Decision logs are sampled earlier with sampling_key=session_id, while trace spans are sampled by the trace sampler which uses trace_id. If the override header is only visible later, decision logs won't reflect the final effective route.

infra-bot: route-eval-sampled | route: gen-default | sampled: 0.05 | window: 2026-02-18T09:05:00Z - 2026-02-18T09:10:00Z

Sam: Quick query I ran against the decision_logs table to correlate (BigQuery):
```sql
SELECT dl.request_id, dl.sampling_key, dl.selected_model, meta.headers['x-routing-override'] as override, ts
FROM prod_decision_logs dl
WHERE ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-02-18T09:00:00Z') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-02-18T09:15:00Z')
ORDER BY ts DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
Result: ~40% of entries have empty override but traces show override present.

Tasha: So we have three entangled issues: (1) decision logs emitted before header-override applied, (2) sampling key doesn't include header-derived bits so correlated trace vs decision_log lookups miss, (3) traces lack a stable link to decision logs (trace_id currently not bubbled into decision logs).

Mike: Propose short-term mitigation: for the next 10m increase decision_log sampling rate to 100% for the affected route and enable a temporary feature-flag to emit decision logs after header-override branch for this route only. This avoids backfill while we patch. Longer term: change sampling_key to include a stable routing fingerprint: `route_id + hash(x-routing-override)` and add `trace_id` to decision log records.

Olivia: Agree. Also we should update the routing middleware to set a `pre_decision_override` flag if an override header exists and emit that into the early decision log, so we at least know an override existed even if final model selection happens later. That helps dashboards and alerts.

Tasha: For backfill: we can re-run history by reprocessing raw request logs where `x-routing-override` present and join them to traces by request_id, then rewrite enriched decision_logs with trace_id. Sam, can you estimate cost for reprocess 15m window?

Sam: Backfill estimate: ~1200 CPU-minutes, ~45GB tmp storage, will take ~30-45 mins with our cluster. I'll open a batch job and tag it `route-eval-backfill-20260218`.

eng-platform-oncall: I'll create a PR with the temporary feature-flag and a console toggle to bump sampling for the single route. Also adding a Grafana panel: ratio(decision_logs_with_override / traces_with_override) over time.

Mike: Small note — when we change sampling_key we must coordinate with metric ingestion (cost, throughput) and update the rollout UI doc so PMs know sampling granularity changed.

Tasha: Thanks all. Action items: Sam -> backfill job, eng-platform-oncall -> PR + console toggle, Mike -> design doc for sampling_key change, Olivia -> update routing middleware to set pre_decision_override. I'll monitor the dashboard and post results here in 20m. :eyes:

infra-bot: deploy job queued: route-eval-flag-toggle (#3421).

Tasha: Update — after enabling 100% sampling for 5m we saw decision_log/trace alignment go to ~98%. Looks like this plan will work. Will follow-up with a small postmortem later. :thumbsup:
